raw_response:
I’m 65 now, so I don’t chase fancy new ways. I look at what worked on my own land, what the neighbors are doing, and what I can afford without making the family too tight on cash. This year I’ll still keep the wheat-maize rotation on part of the land, because that gives steady grain and spreads the risk. Cotton I’ll keep because I know how to manage it, and garlic brings cash, but garlic costs more up front for seed, so I won’t expand it too much. With 14 mu total and some people working off-farm, I have to keep the work and spending balanced. I have a well, so for wheat and garlic I won’t let them suffer badly from dry spells, but I also won’t pump water too many times because electricity and water both cost money. For fertilizer, the extension guy usually talks about standard rates, but on my fields I still go a little by crop appearance and past yield. I’d rather not cut fertilizer too hard, because if wheat or maize turns yellow, that loss is bigger than saving a little money. So this year I’ll keep things fairly steady, with only small adjustments, and I’ll leave some cash in hand instead of pushing everything for maximum yield.
